dedupe_keys.name: dmsp particle precipitation ai ready data machine learning benchmark

description: This dataset is a curated, machine-learning-ready table of electron particle precipitation measured by the SSJ instruments on Defense Meteorological Satellite Program (DMSP) satellites, joined with solar wind and geomagnetic driver parameters. It accompanies the paper by McGranaghan and others on mesoscale prediction of particle precipitation through machine learning, submitted to the AGU journal Space Weather, and was used to train new models of energy flux from the magnetosphere into the ionosphere. It was published in two parts: to allow reuse and extension of the research, and to serve as an AI-ready challenge dataset following a community definition of AI-ready data. It comes as one CSV file (version 1.0.0-alpha of 2021) under CC BY 4.0 from Ryan McGranaghan, Téo Bloch, Jack Ziegler, Spencer Hatch and others. Caveats: it covers the DMSP orbits and years chosen by the authors, it is an alpha release, and driver parameters are pre-selected. It supports training and benchmarking of auroral precipitation models that drive HF absorption, GNSS scintillation and ionospheric conductance inputs for ground-induced current studies; a related record is the NOAA POES and MetOp SEM data.
